title: A Sick Day Without Guilt
script: Maya: [reflective] Lukman, you sound worse than yesterday. Are you still planning to come to the office?
Lukman: I was. We have the client call, and I do not want the team to think I am unreliable.
Maya: [thoughtful] You have a fever and a strong cough. Working in the shared room could also affect other people.
Lukman: I know, but calling in sick always makes me feel guilty.
Maya: [tired] Being responsible includes knowing when rest and medical advice are needed. Have you checked the company policy?
Lukman: It says I should inform the manager before eight and move urgent tasks to a teammate.
Maya: [honestly] Then do that now. I can lead the client call if you send me the latest note.
Lukman: The note is in the shared folder. I need to add one pricing question and the client's new deadline.
Maya: [gently] Send those details, but do not spend two hours making the document perfect.
Lukman: You are right. I will write a short handover and message the manager.
Maya: [hopeful] Do you have someone who can help if you need medicine or food?
Lukman: My brother lives nearby. I will ask him, and I will contact the clinic if the fever continues or warning symptoms appear.
Maya: [relieved] Good. Please do not join the call from bed just to prove commitment.
Lukman: I was thinking about that. It would probably delay my recovery and make the call difficult.
Maya: [grateful] Exactly. A clear handover is more useful than being present without enough strength.
Lukman: I will turn off work notifications after the manager confirms.
Maya: [carefully] The team can handle one day. When someone else is sick, you would want them to recover too.
Lukman: That is true. I do not judge coworkers for using sick leave, only myself.
Maya: [warmly] Then apply the same fairness to yourself.
Lukman: All right. I will send the handover, seek appropriate care, and rest without pretending that illness is a moral failure.

quiz.question: What symptoms does Lukman have?
quiz.explanation: Maya hears and names clear illness signs.

quiz.question: Why does he want to work?
quiz.explanation: Guilt and reputation are influencing him.

quiz.question: What does the policy require?
options: Notify the manager and hand over urgent work
quiz.explanation: The workplace has a clear absence process.

quiz.question: Who can lead the client call?
What does Lukman decide?
options: Write a perfect report all day
Send a short handover, seek care, and rest
quiz.explanation: Responsible absence protects recovery and coworkers.

quiz.question: Why is office attendance not only a personal choice?
options: A shared room could expose coworkers
The client requires a video call
quiz.explanation: Illness may affect others as well as Lukman.

quiz.question: What makes Maya’s help operationally useful?
options: She can lead the call using current shared notes
She promises the client a new price
She writes two hours of detail

quiz.question: Why should the handover remain short?
options: Recovery should not be delayed by perfectionism

quiz.question: What health boundary does Lukman set?
options: Contact the clinic if fever continues or warning signs appear
Assume one rest day is enough
quiz.explanation: The plan includes qualified care and escalation.

quiz.question: What unfair double standard does Lukman notice?
options: He expects Maya to work while ill
He accepts coworkers’ sick leave but judges his own
He applies policy only to managers
quiz.explanation: Maya helps him apply the same fairness inward.
